set_aside.subject: admission evaluation
set_aside.text: Admission is one recorded verdict over the whole active corpus
set_aside.question: When an implementation can produce different outputs across executions, how many times and in what order must each corpus case be executed to produce the recorded admission verdict?
options: Execute each case once and aggregate those results
Execute cases repeatedly under a specified rule before deciding
Reuse existing trial evidence instead of executing cases during admission
set_aside.default_guess: Execute every active case once in a stable order and admit only if every execution passes.

witness.initial: A contract has one trial case, and its implementation obtains chance through an undetected mechanism so the case sometimes passes and sometimes fails.
events: An authoring agent submits the implementation.
The kernel performs admission over the active corpus.
outcomes: A kernel executing the case once records admitted after a passing execution and activates the implementation.
A kernel requiring repeated consistent passes records refused after a later failing execution.
witness.observer: The agent sees a different admission result and the flow either can or cannot use the implementation.

set_aside.subject: recorded admission verdict identity
set_aside.text: Admission is one recorded verdict over the whole active corpus
set_aside.question: What identifies the corpus covered by a recorded verdict, and what happens to that verdict and its activation when a trial case is subsequently added?
options: Key the verdict to an exact corpus revision and mark it stale when the corpus changes while leaving the existing activation in place
Invalidate the verdict and deactivate the implementation when the corpus changes
Treat the verdict as permanently attached to the implementation despite later corpus changes
set_aside.default_guess: Key the verdict to the exact corpus contents; adding a case makes it stale for rollback or future activation but does not revoke an activation already in use.

witness.initial: Implementation I is admitted and active after passing corpus C1.
events: An authoring agent adds a new valid case, producing corpus C2.
The owner inspects I's verdict and attempts to roll the slot back to I after another implementation has become active.
outcomes: The stored verdict is still treated as admitted, so rollback to I succeeds without testing the new case.
The verdict is stale because it covered C1 rather than C2, so rollback is refused until I is admitted over C2.
witness.observer: The owner sees whether rollback succeeds and which implementation becomes active.

set_aside.subject: resubmission of an identical implementation
set_aside.text: Admission is one recorded verdict over the whole active corpus
set_aside.question: If the same immutable implementation is submitted again against an unchanged corpus, must the kernel return its existing recorded verdict or execute admission again and record another verdict?
options: Memoize and return the existing verdict
Run a new admission attempt and retain each attempt's verdict
Run again but replace the prior recorded verdict
set_aside.default_guess: Return the existing verdict for the same implementation and exact corpus revision.

witness.initial: A nondeterministic implementation was previously refused after failing the unchanged corpus; its content identity therefore already exists.
events: The authoring agent submits exactly the same implementation content again.
outcomes: The kernel returns the recorded refusal without executing it again.
The kernel executes admission again, happens to pass, records admission and activates it.
witness.observer: The agent sees refusal versus admission, and later runs see a different active implementation.
